sections.html:
Clayton County runs along the Mississippi River in Iowa's northeast corner, with Elkader as seat. Nearly everyone lives in the country or a small town, with 99.1 percent of residents counted as rural in 2020. The county counted 17,043 people that year and was estimated at 16,845 in 2025. Postville (2,503), Guttenberg (1,817), Monona (1,471), Elkader (1,209) and Strawberry Point (1,155) are the larger towns.

Homes are valued at a median $168,500, and 78.0 percent of households own. Bluffs, ridges and river valleys make the terrain uneven, which means flood and weather exposure can differ sharply between two nearby houses.

Insurance questions follow any house with a flood past. Record crests were set on the Turkey River at Elkader on June 10, 2008 (27.77 feet, against a 12 foot flood stage) and on the Mississippi at Guttenberg on April 24, 1965 (23.65 feet, against 15). Guttenberg's riverfront has flooded many times, and a levee went up after 1965.

Hail and wind also matter. Since 1982 there have been 102 reports of large hail and 104 of damaging wind, so an older roof draws questions from buyers. Look up the property's flood zone before listing, and collect roof and repair paperwork for the buyer.

sections.h2: Where to pay and who to call
sections.html:
Everything property related happens in Elkader. Go to the Treasurer at 111 High Street NE, Suite 102, IA 52043, call 563-245-1106, and plan on weekday hours between 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

The county site lists a second building at 600 Gunder Road NE. Reach the assessor through the county contact page. The division of labor is simple: the assessor values, the auditor figures levies, and the treasurer collects.

sections.h2: Installments, penalties and the tax sale
sections.html:
The county splits your bill into September 1 and March 1 installments. Fall half penalties begin October 1, or 30 days after the auditor certifies to the treasurer when that comes later, and spring half penalties begin April 1.

Clayton County penalty and tax sale charges
ChargeClayton County amount or rule
Penalty rate1 1/2% per month on real estate tax
Tax saleThird Monday in June, 1:00 p.m.
Advertising fee$4.00 per attached description
Certificate fee if sold$10.00
Redemption interest2% per month, minimum $1.00

Mailing a payment? Iowa Code 445.37 wants it in the treasurer's hands by the last business day of the month before delinquency, or postmarked before that date.

Outside agriculture, property is assessed at full market value on January 1. Odd numbered years bring a complete reassessment, and notices are due by April 15. A farmhouse is valued like any house, farm land is valued by output, and mobile homes are taxed by the square foot.

Protests are accepted April 2 through April 30, as Iowa Code 441.37 provides. The board sits during May, and an equalization order that shifts values brings it back from October 15 to November 15.

You can argue unequal treatment, a value over market, a misclassified or exempt property, or a mistake. If the ruling disappoints, the Property Assessment Appeal Board is next, with district court after it, and the clock is 20 days from the postmark on your appeal letter. Skipping the appeal board is possible too: file in district court within 20 days after adjournment or by May 31, whichever comes later.

sections.h2: Closing day and the tax bill
sections.html:
Buyer and seller typically split the year's tax by proration, and the settlement sheet displays each share. Because statements go to the titleholder of record, a seller should pass along any bill that shows up after the sale.

Iowa's transfer tax is 80 cents on every $500 beyond the first $500. A declaration of value, signed by either party, accompanies the deed and then sits with the assessor for three years.

Back taxes are best cleared before June, because once a certificate sells, 2 percent monthly interest and fees join the payoff.

First, ask the treasurer what is owed and whether any half is already late. Second, find out whether the parcel is on the advertised list, since the advertising fee and the certificate fee both land on a parcel that sells. Third, confirm what the assessor has on file for buildings, because a deck, garage or addition that was never reported will surprise a buyer. Fourth, pull flood and insurance paperwork if the house is near the Turkey River or the Mississippi. Finally, send the title company a payoff figure so the tax comes out of proceeds at closing. If a bill reaches you after the sale, forward it, since the county mails to whoever held title when the statement was issued.

Clayton County houses range from river town limestone buildings to rural farmhouses, and many need roofs, wiring or foundation attention. Sellers who would rather not manage repairs can sell for cash as-is. The tax steps stay the same either way: confirm the balance, clear any penalty, and let the title company settle the county's share at the table.

The June 2008 flood followed 3 to 7 inches of rain over two days, closed roads with mudslides and caused more than $10 million in property damage. Beyond floods, the county has recorded 14 tornadoes since 1950, among them an F3 west of Elkader on May 30, 1985, and Elkader's snowfall averages about 37 inches a season.

None of this stops a sale, but buyers and their insurers ask about it. If your house sits low near a creek or river, having an elevation certificate or insurance history ready shortens the conversation and keeps the closing on track, and it signals to a buyer that the house has been looked after.

sections.h2: What to bring to the treasurer's window
sections.html:
Bring the parcel number or the property address, last year's statement if you have it, and a closing date or a rough one. With those, staff can quote what is owed on each installment, including any penalty already running, and tell you whether the parcel has been advertised for the June sale. If you are selling an inherited house, bring whatever document shows you can act for the owner, since the office will want to know who is asking. Ask for the figure in writing, and ask how long it stays good, because the penalty grows monthly and a number quoted today will be too low in a few weeks.

A seller who lives out of the area can usually handle this by phone at 563-245-1106 and then pass the figure to the title company.

faqs.q: When are Clayton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first installment is due September 1 and the second March 1. Penalties of 1 1/2 percent a month start the following October 1 and April 1.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Clayton County?
faqs.a: Go to the County Treasurer in Elkader, 111 High Street NE, Suite 102, or call 563-245-1106 on a weekday between 8:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: When is the Clayton County tax sale?
faqs.a: Third Monday of June, 1:00 p.m. Parcels pay a $4.00 advertising fee ahead of the sale, plus $10.00 per certificate if one sells.

faqs.q: What is the protest deadline in Clayton County?
faqs.a: The window opens April 2 and closes April 30 under Iowa Code 441.37.
Record floods hit the Turkey River at Elkader in June 2008 and the Mississippi at Guttenberg in April 1965. Check a property's flood zone before you list.
